rated_messages.input_message: Use self-talk to stay motivated and determined. Say, “I don't need a cigarette. I might WANT one, but I don’t NEED it.”
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.
When a craving hits, keep your hands busy by doing the dishes or taking out the trash. Small chores will help pass the time during a craving.
Some places trigger powerful cravings, that is to be expected. Stop and notice where in your body you feel those cravings and remind yourself that cravings typically pass in 1 to 3 minutes
Stress is temporary. It comes and goes like passing clouds in the sky. When stress demands you to light up, remember you can let it pass by without smoking.
Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.

Don't let anyone tell you how you should or shouldn't feel today. You feel how you feel and that's it. If you're happy and grateful then enjoy the moment, if you're angry and frustrated, know that this will pass.
A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"

Pause. Notice the feelings you are having without judgement. Let them come and go. Being aware of your feelings means you can make a new choice about how you respond to your urges instead of smoking on autopilot.

Think about a happy memory to ease the difficulty of your urge. Is there something you have been wanting to do for a while that you know you would enjoy? Reading? Walking? Calling a friend? Doing a puzzle? Do something that matters to you instead of smoking.
